Aquí llega lo que distingue al cálculo n: Here is what distinguishes numerical computation from mere programming. A computer does not store exact numbers but approximations with a few digits, so every operation introduces a minute error. The issue is not that the error exists, but how it behaves as it accumulates over millions of operations: if it is kept in check, the result is usable; if it is amplified, the result is rubbish with the look of a number.

Durante décadas, los cálculos numéricos: For decades, the numerical computations of aeronautics were done by people. At the Langley centre of the agency that would later be NASA there worked a team of African American women mathematicians, segregated from the rest. Dorothy Vaughan, who led it, saw the first IBM computers arrive and taught herself FORTRAN so as to teach it to her team before the machines put them out of work. Katherine Johnson computed by hand the trajectories of the first crewed missions, checked those of the first American orbital flight and took part in the computations for the Apollo 11 journey to the Moon. Their story became famous in 2016 with the book and the film Hidden Figures.
El <strong>análisis numérico</strong> es: Numerical analysis is the discipline that answers: if I cannot solve it exactly, I approximate it as closely as I like, and I also prove how far wrong I am. It is what any calculator, simulator or physics engine does on the inside.
El cálculo numérico es tan antiguo como: Numerical computation is as old as mathematics: there is a Babylonian tablet, YBC 7289, from some 3700 years ago, giving the value of $\sqrt{2}$ to a precision of six decimal places. The method they used is the same one taught today as a particular case of Newton's. That is, someone was applying it three thousand years before Newton was born.
El ejemplo llega a $[1{,}5,\\ 1{,}625]$: The example reaches $[1{.}5,\ 1{.}625]$ in three steps. How many steps will be needed for the guaranteed error to drop below 0.001? Think how many times 1 has to be halved.
El error numérico ha costado vidas. En 1: Numerical error has cost lives. In 1991, a Patriot battery failed to intercept a missile at Dhahran and 28 people died: the internal clock was accumulating a minute rounding error which, after a hundred hours switched on, had become a third of a second, enough to miss the target by half a kilometre. In 1996, the Ariane 5 destroyed itself 37 seconds in because of a numerical conversion that overflowed. Studying error is not academic pedantry.
El método de Newton es el que ejecuta tu: Newton's method is the one your calculator runs when you press the square root key, and the one that solves, on the inside, almost any equation with no formula. Its speed —each step doubles the correct digits— is what lets a structural simulator or a circuit program solve millions of non-linear equations in seconds. Its weak point, losing its way if the derivative is small, is the reason serious programs combine it with bisection.
El método de los trapecios sustituye la: The trapezium method replaces the curve by segments; Simpson's, by parabolas, and that is why it is far more accurate for the same effort.
